title: The Black Museum
paragraphs: Orson Welles narrates dramatizations of British murder cases, each introduced through an object preserved in Scotland Yard's Black Museum and used as the doorway into the crime story.

Syndicated true-crime radio anthology hosted and narrated by Orson Welles, using objects associated with cases from Scotland Yard's Black Museum as dramatic frames. Source logs explicitly warn that surviving titles, program numbers, and broadcast order vary; no episode-specific 1952 airdate is imposed.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1952 U.S. Mutual/syndication circulation (January 1, 1952 to December 30, 1952) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Harry Alan Towers (producer), Ira Marion (writer), [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] (narrator), and Sidney Torch (composer and conductor).

The stories often return to crime-associated museum artifact, murder and homicide investigation, Scotland Yard and criminal investigation, forensic and physical evidence, clothing, textiles and personal effects, and documents, messages and written clues.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Scotland Yard Crime Museum case-artifact framing, International transcription syndication, Stable production team, and Title and order instability in syndicated preservation.
